name: branch-on-verdict

nodes.goal: You are a judge. Decide ONE verdict for this statement: 'The number 17 is prime.' Reply with ONLY a fenced json block: {"verdict": "ship" | "hold", "why": "<one line>"}. Use 'ship' when the statement is true.
The go-arm ran because the judge said ship. Under '## Inputs' you have the judge's verdict. Reply with ONLY a fenced json block: {"arm": "go", "echo": "<the judge's why>"}.
The hold-arm ran because the judge said hold and the owner released the gate. Reply with ONLY a fenced json block: {"arm": "hold"}.

You are the join. Under '## Inputs' you have the judge's verdict; both arm dependencies are terminal, but exactly one is skipped. If verdict is ship, reply with ONLY a fenced json block {"arms_seen": ["ship_it"]}; otherwise reply {"arms_seen": ["escalate"]}. For a real join needing the live arm's output, read its committed nodes/<arm>.json record from the run directory (do not require inputs from a possibly pruned arm).

description: Two-arm branch on a schema'd verdict: complementary `when` gates with on_skip:prune; the dead arm is pruned (skipped, not run); the join runs on the live arm only. Replace judge/ship_it/escalate goals with real work.
